business_profile.description: Production of jowar-based Jolada Rotti using semi-automated rotti pressing machines, dough mixer and gas puffing bhatti. Rotti made from locally sourced jowar flour, packed in hygienic packaging with short shelf life (8-12 hours for fresh, 3 days with vacuum packing). Business leverages Kalaburagi district's 90% rainfed jowar cultivation and the existing Kalaburagi Rotti Sahakara Sanga cooperative model where SHGs earn Rs 250-300 per day supplying rottis at Rs 5 to cooperative that retails at Rs 7.

rural_suitability.reason: Kalaburagi has jowar as major crop per NABARD PLP and NDMA district profile; staple food; low skill women SHG model proven with 150 roti-making machines distributed at subsidized rate; district ODOP under PMFME is Toor Dal based products but millets promoted under Raitha Siri; Kalaburagi Rotti brand launched March 2024 and listed on Zomato/Swiggy

financial_model.calculation_methodology: Monthly Revenue = Rottis per day * Avg price Rs 7.5 * Working days 26. Monthly Expenses = Raw material (rottis per day * 0.08 kg * Rs 35 * 26) + Labour (1 person small 300*26=7800, 2 persons medium 15600, 5 persons large 39000) + LPG (2-6 cylinders) + Rent + Electricity 1000-3000 + Packaging + Transport + Loan interest if PMEGP/Mudra. Profit = Revenue - Expenses. Break-even = Initial Investment / Monthly Operating Profit. Small: 285000/22000=12.95 months ~13. Medium: 650000/60000=10.8 ~11. Large: 1350000/195000=6.9 ~7.

strengths: Abundant local raw material - jowar major crop per NABARD PLP 2020-21 and Karnataka jowar area 6.48 lakh ha with Kalaburagi as major district

Low margin at Rs 5 purchase to Rs 7 retail - only Rs 2 margin for cooperative, need volume
opportunities: Online delivery - Kalaburagi Rotti listed on Zomato/Swiggy per Indian Express, GeM MoU 14 Nov 2024 for PMFME branding support
Export - Thousands of rottis exported monthly to US, Canada, Australia per Asianet Newsable - premium pricing

Institutional sales - Hostels, industrial canteens, base kitchens, nursing homes per JK Engineering machine market segments
FPO linkage - 14 FPOs supported by NABARD in Kalaburagi district plus Aland Bhootai Millets and Jewaragi Taluka Millets FPOs for bulk flour supply
threats: Area under jowar declining - transition probability matrix shows sugarcane retaining 40% and gaining 38% from Jowar area 2011-12 to 2020-21
Competition from rice/wheat shift due to urbanization per DC Fouzia Taranum statement
Price volatility - Jowar MSP Rs 3371 (2024-25) to Rs 3699 (2025-26) but open market Rs 2500-8000 swing during drought
Climate - Semiarid, 90% rainfed, drought, heat wave 41.8°C, water conservation thrust needed in Aland, Afzalpur, Sedam

seven_day_validation_experiment.objective: Validate demand, supply, competition and unit economics for semi-automated Jolada Rotti in chosen taluk before investing Rs 2.85 lakh

days.activity: Study competitors and local market in Kalaburagi city Appa Lake outlet and Aland/Afzalpur/Jevargi weekly santhe
days.target: Visit 5 khanavalis, 2 APMC canteens, 1 cooperative outlet
days.measurement: Note price Rs 7-10 per rotti, daily sales volume, hygiene gaps

days.activity: Interview 20 potential customers (households, hostel wardens, hotel owners)
days.measurement: Ask willingness to buy at Rs 7-8, frequency daily/weekly, preference fresh vs vacuum packed

days.activity: Contact suppliers for jowar flour and machine
days.target: 3 flour mills/APMC traders, 2 machine suppliers (Jas Enterprise, JK Engineering via TradeIndia)
days.measurement: Get quotation: machine Rs 80k-2.5 lakh, flour Rs 32-38 per kg, delivery terms

days.activity: Test product - make 50 rottis manually or with rented machine with SHG woman
days.measurement: Record flour used kg, time taken, LPG consumption, taste feedback from 10 persons

days.activity: Attempt actual sales/pre-orders - take to bus stand, APMC, 2 hotels
days.measurement: Number sold, time to sell, repeat purchase intention, rejection reasons

days.target: Compute cost per rotti = (flour 80g*35 + LPG + labour + packaging)
days.measurement: If cost per rotti < Rs 5.5 and selling Rs 7.5, margin > Rs 2 acceptable; compute break-even days
Proceed if >=10 customer interviews positive, >=50 pre-orders, margin >= Rs 2, supplier confirmed. Modify if need packaging change. Do Not Proceed if <5 interested or cost > Rs 6.5 per rotti

success_criteria: At least 15 customer interviews with 60% willingness to buy at Rs 7-8
At least 80 out of 100 test rottis sold within 4 hours
Supplier quotation with flour at <= Rs 38 per kg and machine at <= Rs 1.5 lakh for base model
At least 2 B2B leads (hotel/hostel/canteen) for daily 100+ rottis
failure_criteria: Cost per rotti > Rs 6.5 making margin negative vs Rs 7 price
No supplier for jowar flour within 20 km
Machine cost > Rs 3 lakh without subsidy
seven_day_validation_experiment.decision_rule: Proceed if success criteria met 4/5, Modify if 3/5 met (change location to Kalaburagi city or add bajra), Do Not Proceed if <2 met

government_schemes.scheme_selection_method: Select the five most relevant currently applicable schemes based on verified business eligibility and financial relevance - PMFME for food processing, PMEGP for micro enterprise, Stand-Up India for women/SC/ST greenfield loan, Raitha Siri for millet raw material security, Udyogini for Karnataka women micro credit. All verified from official PIB, NABARD, KSWDC, The Hindu BusinessLine.

capital_and_financing.recommended_funding_pathway: Small scale: Own 10% Rs 35000 + PMFME credit-linked subsidy 35% max Rs 10 lakh (Rs 99750 on Rs 285k) + Bank loan Rs 185250 via Mudra Tarun (up to Rs 10 lakh) or PMEGP (if women/SC/ST 35% subsidy better). For women: Use Udyogini 30% (Rs 85500) or 50% SC/ST plus Stand-Up India if scaling to Rs 10 lakh. For medium: PMFME Rs 10 lakh ceiling + Stand-Up India Rs 10 lakh-1 crore composite. Register Udyam and FSSAI first, then approach DIC Kalaburagi with DPR via DRP handholding under PMFME.
capital_and_financing.important_distinction: Business investment and government-scheme own contribution are different concepts.

final_feasibility.strongest_reason_to_consider: Kalaburagi taluk has verified high demand with city population 533,587, Kalaburagi Rotti brand established March 2024 with 150 subsidized machines at Rs 2 lakh (vs market Rs 5-10 lakh), 3000+ rottis per day production, first outlet near Appa Lake, franchise plan to Bengaluru/Hyderabad, Zomato/Swiggy listing, export to US/Canada/Australia, plus PMFME 35% subsidy up to Rs 10 lakh and strong APMC and banking infrastructure 271 branches
final_feasibility.biggest_risk: Raw material jowar area declining 38% shifted to sugarcane per transition matrix and price volatility Rs 2500-8000 per quintal during drought plus semiarid climate 750-842 mm erratic rainfall and water scarcity in Aland/Afzalpur thrust areas
final_feasibility.minimum_viable_startup: Small scale 400 rottis per day with one semi-automatic press at Rs 2.85 lakh total investment, working capital Rs 35k, break-even 13 months, monthly profit expected Rs 22k
final_feasibility.recommended_scale_for_beginner: Small scale SHG model linked to Kalaburagi Rotti Sahakara Sanga - buy subsidized machine at Rs 2 lakh, supply to cooperative at Rs 5 per rotti earning Rs 250-300 per day as per existing model, then scale to medium after validation
final_feasibility.recommended_validation_before_investment: 7-day validation experiment: visit Appa Lake outlet, interview 15 customers, get machine and flour quotations, test 50 rottis, attempt 100 pre-orders, calculate unit cost < Rs 5.5 vs selling Rs 7.5
final_feasibility.loan_readiness: Ready for Mudra Tarun up to Rs 10 lakh (enhanced to Rs 20 lakh for Tarun Plus from Oct 2024) and PMFME 35% subsidy and PMEGP 35% for women/SC/ST rural - requires Udyam and FSSAI and DPR via DRP
final_feasibility.overall_data_confidence: Medium - core facts verified from NABARD PLP, PIB PMFME/PMEGP/Mudra, The Hindu/Indian Express Kalaburagi Rotti initiative, citypopulation.de census, NDMA climate; financial projections estimated with transparent assumptions
